title: 1952 AHSME Problem 42
statement: Let \(D\) represent a repeating decimal. If \(P\) denotes the \(r\) figures of \(D\) which do not repeat themselves, and \(Q\) denotes the \(s\) figures which do repeat themselves, then the incorrect expression is:

solutions.text:
After shifting past the nonrepeating block, \[ 10^rD=P.QQQ\ldots, \] and after shifting one repeating block farther, \[ 10^{r+s}D=PQ.QQQ\ldots. \] Subtracting yields the standard relation \[ \begin{gathered} 10^r(10^s-1)D \\ =P(10^s-1)+Q. \end{gathered} \] This is not \(Q(P-1),\) as stated in choice D.

Thus, the incorrect expression, and hence the correct answer, is D.
hints: Shift the decimal point first past the \(r\) nonrepeating digits and then past one block of \(s\) repeating digits
Subtract \(10^rD\) from \(10^{r+s}D\) and compare the result with choice D
